title: Board Policy 2023-07: the expectation that Board-licensed pharmacies engage in non-sterile compounding, and the Board's examples of complex non-sterile compounding
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2023-07, Non-Sterile Compounding, describes itself as an overview of requirements for non-sterile compounding by Board-licensed pharmacies that is not intended to be an exhaustive list, and states that licensees are expected to adhere to the United States Pharmacopeia (USP) and any state and federal requirements, and that, except for complex non-sterile compounding, all pharmacies licensed by the Board are expected to engage in non-sterile compounding in accordance with Board regulations. It states that an additional pharmacy specialty license is required to prepare and dispense complex non-sterile preparations into, within, or from Massachusetts, and that the Board considers the following to be examples of complex non-sterile compounding, not all inclusive: compounding of NIOSH drug containing preparations or other hazardous agents; use of complex calculations such as accounting for loss on drying, salt conversions and multiple aliquots; and preparation of transdermal dosage forms, capsules, suppositories, troches, lollipops, sublingual dosage forms, tablets, tablet triturates, modified-release preparations, and other dosage forms intended to deliver systemic effects. It also states that simple reconstitution of FDA approved, conventionally manufactured non-sterile drug products in accordance with manufacturer package insert instructions is not considered compounding, and that flavoring agents added to conventionally manufactured non-sterile drug products is considered compounding.
exam_relevance: Tests the Board's stated expectation that every Board-licensed pharmacy engages in non-sterile compounding other than complex non-sterile compounding, and the Board's examples that place a request inside or outside the complex category.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2023-07: Non-Sterile Compounding
authority.section: Policy 2023-07, introduction and sections III.B, III.C, VII.A and VII.B

exceptions: The expectation to engage in non-sterile compounding is stated except for complex non-sterile compounding.
common_confusions: The policy states an expectation in Board guidance; the prohibition on refusing to compound is the regulation in 247 CMR 9.01(15).
The Board's list of examples of complex non-sterile compounding is expressly not all inclusive.

Adding a flavoring agent to a conventionally manufactured non-sterile drug product is compounding under the policy, while simple reconstitution in accordance with the manufacturer package insert instructions is not.
